verses.text: Therfore God hath deliuered them into paſsions of ignominie. For their vvomen haue changed the natural vſe, into that vſe that is contrarie to nature.

And in like maner the men alſo, leauing the natural vſe of the woman, haue burned in their deſires one tovvard an other, men vpon men vvorking turpitude, & the revvard of their errour (vvhich they ſhould) receauing in them ſelues.
And as they liked not to haue God in knovvledge: God deliuered them vp into a reprobate ſenſe: to doe thoſe things that are not conuenient:
repleniſhed vvith al iniquitie, malice, fornication, auarice, vvickednes, ful of enuie, murder, contention, guile, malignitie, vvhiſperers,
detractours, odible to God, contumelious, proude, hautie, inuentours of euil things, diſobedient to parents,
foliſh, diſſolute, vvithout affection, vvithout fidelitie, vvithout mercie.
Who vvhereas they knevv the iuſtice of God, did not vnderſtand that they vvhich doe ſuch things, are vvorthie of death: not only they that doe them, but they alſo that conſent to the doers.

chapters.summary: The foundation of his Apoſtleſhip being laid, 8 he highly commendeth the Romanes, and proteſteth his affection tovvardes them. and ſo comming to the matter, ſaith, our Chriſtian Catholike doctrine (that teacheth al to beleeue) to be the vvay to ſaluation: 18 becauſe the Gentiles (firſt of al) could not be ſaued by their Philoſophie, whereby they knew God, for ſo much as they did not ſerue him, but Idols: he therfore iuſtly permitting them to fall into al kind of moſt damnable ſinne.

verses.text: <sc>FOR</sc> the vvhich cauſe thou art inexcuſable ô man vvhoſoeuer thou be that iudgeſt. For vvherein thou iudgeſt an other, thou condemneſt thy ſelf. for thou doeſt the ſame things vvhich thou iudgeſt.
For vve knovv that the iudgement of God is according to veritie vpon them that doe ſuch things.
And doeſt thou ſuppoſe this ô man that iudgeſt them which doe ſuch things, and doeſt the ſame, that thou ſhalt eſcape the iudgement of God?
Or doeſt thou contemne the riches of his goodnes, and patience, and longanimity, not knovving that the benignity of God bringeth thee to penance?
But according to thy hardnes and impenitent hart, thou heapeſt to thy ſelf vvrath, in the day of vvrath and of the reuelation of the iuſt iudgement of God,
vvho vvil <cr>[1]</cr> render to euery man according to his vvorkes.
<na>[1]</na> to them truely that according to patience in good vvorke, ſeeke glorie and honour and incorruption, life eternal.

notes.text: Good men alſo according to the merits of their good vvil ſhal haue their reward. Aug. ep. 47. · Pſal. 61, 13.

verses.text: but to them that are of contention, and that obey not the truth, but giue credite to iniquitie, vvrath and indignation.
Tribulation and anguiſh vpon euery ſoul of man that vvorketh euil, of the Ievve firſt and of the <na>[1]</na> Greeke:

notes.text: c That is, the Gentile.

verses.text: but glorie and honour and peace to euery one that vvorketh good, to the Ievv firſt and to the Greeke.
for <cr>[1]</cr> there is no acception of perſons vvith God.
For vvhoſoeuer haue ſinned vvithout the Lavv, vvhithout the Lavv ſhal periſh: and vvhoſoeuer haue ſinned in the Lavv, by the Lavv ſhal be iudged.
For <cr>[1]</cr> not the hearers of the Lavv are iuſt vvith God: but the doers of the Lavv ſhal be iuſtified.
For vvhen the Gentiles vvhich haue not the Lavv, naturally doe thoſe things that are of the Lavv: the ſame not hauing the Lavv, them ſelues are a lavv to them ſelues:
vvho ſhevv the vvorke of the Lavv vvritten in their hartes, their conſcience giuing teſtimonie to them, and among them ſelues mutually their thoughtes accuſing, or alſo defending,
in the day vvhen God ſhal iudge the ſecretes of men, according to my Goſpel, by <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc>.
But if thou be ſurnamed a Ievv, and reſteſt in the Lavv, and doeſt glorie in God,
and knovveſt his vvil, and approueſt the more profitable things, inſtructed by the Lavv,
preſumeſt that thy ſelf art a leader of the blinde, a light of them that are in darknes,
a teacher of the foliſh, a maiſter of infants, hauing the forme of ſcience & of veritie in the Lavv.
Thou therfore <na>[1]</na> that teacheſt an other, teacheſt not thy ſelf: that preacheſt, men ought not to ſteale, thou ſtealeſt:

notes.text: It is a ſhameful and damnable thing for preachers, teachers, or other guides of mens life, to commit the ſame things them ſelues which they reproue in other.

verses.text: that ſaieſt men ſhould not commit aduoutrie, thou committeſt aduoutrie: that abhorreſt idols, thou doeſt ſacrilege:
that doeſt glorie in the Lavv, thou by preuarication of the Lavv doeſt diſhonour God. (
[1] For [2] the name of God through you is blaſphemed among the Gentiles, as it is vvriten.)

notes.text: c It is a great ſinne that by the il life of the faithful, our Lordes name ſhould be il ſpoken of amōg the miſbeleuers, & many withdrawen from the true religiō thereby. · Es. 52, 5. Ez. 36, 20.

verses.text: Circumciſion in deede profiteth, if thou obſerue the Lavv: but if thou be a preuaricatour of the Law, thy circumciſion is become <na>[1]</na> prepuce.

notes.text: Prepuce iſ the foreſkinne not circumciſed, & therfore ſignifieth the Gentiles, or the ſtate and conditiō of the Gentiles: as circumciſiō, the Iewes and their ſtate.

verses.text: If then the prepuce keepe the iuſtices of the Lavv: ſhal not his prepuce be reputed for circumciſion?
and ſhal not that vvhich of nature is prepuce, fulfilling the Lavv, iudge thee, that by the letter and circumciſion art a preuaricatour of the Lavv?
For not he that is in open ſhevv, is a Ievv, nor that vvhich is in open ſhevv, in the fleſh, is circumciſion:
but he that is in ſecrete, is a Ievv: and the circumciſion of the hart, in ſpirit, not in the letter: vvhoſe praiſe is not of men, but of God.

chapters.summary: Now alſo he ſheweth that neither the Iewes could be ſaued by the knovvledge of the Law, of the vvhich they did ſo much bragge againſt the Gentils, ſeing they did notvvithſtanding ſinne as the Gentils did. 14 And therfore that the true Iew is the Chriſtian (though he be a Gentil) vvho by grace in his hart doeth the good workes that the Lavv commaundeth.

verses.text: <sc>WHAT</sc> preeminence then hath the Ievv, or what is the profit of circumciſion?
Much by al meanes. Firſt ſurely becauſe the vvordes of God vvere cōmitted to them.
for vvhat if certaine of them haue not beleeued? Hath their incredulitie made the faith of God fruſtrate?
God forbid. but [1] God is true: & [2][3] euery man a lyer, as it is vvritten: [4] That thou maieſt be iuſtified in thy vvordes, and ouercome vvhen thou art iudged.

notes.text: God only by nature is true, al mere men by nature may lie, deceiue and be deceiued: yet God by his grace & ſpirit may and doth preſerue the Apoſtles and principal gouerners of his people & the Church and Councels in al truth, though they were and are mere men. · Io. 3, 33. Ps. 115, 11. Ps. 50, 6.

verses.text: But if our iniquitie commend the iuſtice of God, vvhat ſhal vve ſay? Is God vniuſt that executeth vvrath? (I ſpeake according to man)
God forbid. othervviſe hovv ſhal God iudge this vvorld?
For if the veritie of God hath abounded in my lie, vnto his glorie, vvhy am I alſo yet iudged as a ſinner,
and not (as vve are blaſphemed, and as ſome report vs to ſay) let vs doe euil, that there may come good? vvhoſe damnation is iuſt.
What then? do vve excel them? No, not ſo. For vve haue argued the Ievves and the Greekes, al to be vnder ſinne:
as it is vvritten: [1] That there is not any man iuſt,
there is not that vnderſtandeth, there is not that ſeeketh after God.
Al haue declined, they are become vnprofitable together: there is not that doeth good, there is not ſo much as one.
[1] Their throte is an open ſepulchre, with their tonges they dealt deceitefully. [2] The venim [3] of aſpes vnder their lippes.

notes.text: c Aſpidum, A kinde of litle ſerpents.

verses.text: [1] Whoſe mouth is ful of malediction and bitternes:
[1] Their feete ſwift to ſhede bloud.
Deſtruction and infelicitie in their vvaies:
and the vvay of peace they haue not knowen.
[1] There is no feare of God before their eies.
And vve knovv that vvhatſoeuer the Lavv ſpeaketh, to them it ſpeaketh that are in the Lavv: that euery mouth may be ſtopped, and al the vvorld may be made ſubiect to God:
becauſe <cr>[1]</cr> by the vvorkes of the Lavv no fleſh ſhal be iuſtified before him. For by the Lavv is the knovvledge of ſinne.
But novv vvithout the Lavv the iuſtice of God is manifeſted: teſtified by the lavv and the Prophets.
And the iuſtice of God by faith of <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc>, vnto al and vpō al that <na>[1]</na> beleeue in him. For there is no diſtinction.

notes.text: c To beleeue in him, here compriſeth not only the act of faith, but of hope & charitie, as the Apoſtle explicateth him ſelf. Galat. 5, 6.

verses.text: For al haue ſinned: and doe neede the glorie of God.
Iuſtified <na>[1]</na> gratis by his grace, by the redemption that is in <sc>CHRIST IESVS</sc>,

notes.text: No man atteineth his firſt Iuſtification by the merites either of his faith or workes, but merely by Chriſtes grace and mercie: though his faith & vvorkes proceding of grace be diſpoſitions & preparations thereunto.

verses.text: vvhom God hath propoſed a <na>[1]</na> <alt>propitiation</alt>, by faith in his bloud, to the ſhevving of his iuſtice, for the remiſſion of former ſinnes,

notes.text: propitiator

verses.text: in the toleration of God, to the ſhevving of his iuſtice in this time: that he may be iuſt, and iuſtifying him that is of the faith of <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc>.
VVhere is then thy boaſting? it is excluded. by vvhat lavv? of deedes? No, but by the lavv of faith.
For we account a man to be iuſtified by faith vvithout the vvorkes of the Lavv.
Is he God of the Iewes only? is he not alſo of the Gentiles? Yes of the Gentiles alſo.
For it is one God, that iuſtifieth circumciſion by faith, and prepuce by faith.
Do vve then deſtroy the Lavv by faith? God forbid. but vve do eſtabliſh the Lavv.

chapters.summary: He graunteth that the Iewes did paſſe the Heathen Gentils, in Gods benefits, 9 but not in their owne vvorkes. concluding, that he hath ſhewed, both Iew and Gentil to be ſinners: 18 and therfore (inferring) that there muſt be ſome other vvay to Saluation, indifferent to both, which is to beleeue in IESVS CHRIST, that for his ſake their ſinnes may be forgiuen them.

verses.text: <sc>WHAT</sc> ſhal vve ſay then that Abraham did finde, our father according to the fleſh?
For if Abraham vvere iuſtified by vvorkes, he hath glorie, but not vvith God.
For vvhat ſaieth the Scripture? [1] Abraham beleeued God, and it vvas reputed him to iuſtice.
But to him that vvorketh, the revvard is not <na>[1]</na> imputed according to grace, but according to dette.

notes.text: c λογίζεται

verses.text: But to him that vvorketh not, yet beleeueth in him that iuſtifieth the impious, his faith is <na>[1]</na> reputed to iuſtice according to the purpoſe of the grace of God.

notes.text: c λογίζεται

verses.text: As Dauid alſo termeth the bleſſednes of a man, to vvhom God reputeth iuſtice vvithout vvorkes:
[1] Bleſſed are they, whoſe iniquities be forgiuen, and vvhoſe ſinnes be couered.
Bleſſed is the man, to vvhom our Lord hath not imputed ſinne.
This bleſſednes then doth it abide in the circumciſion, or in the prepuce alſo? For vve ſay that vnto Abraham faith vvas <na>[1]</na> reputed to iuſtice.

notes.text: The word, Reputed, doth not diminiſh the truth of the iuſtice: as though it were reputed for iuſtice, being not iuſtice in deede. but ſignifieth, that as it was in it ſelf, ſo God eſteemed & reputed it. as the ſame greeke word muſt needes be taken v. 4. next going before, & 1 Cor. 4, 1. and els where.

verses.text: How vvas it reputed? in circumciſion, or in prepuce? Not in circumciſion, but in prepuce.

And <cr>[1]</cr> he receiued <na>[2]</na> the ſigne of circumciſion, a ſeale of the iuſtice of faith that is in prepuce: that he might be the father of al that beleeue by the prepuce, that vnto them alſo it may be reputed to iuſtice:

notes.text: Gen. 17, 10. · Our Sacraments of the new Lavv giue ex opere operato that grace and iuſtice of faith vvhich here is commended. whereas circūciſiō vvas but a ſigne or marke of the ſame.

verses.text: and might be father of circumciſion, not to them only that are of the circumciſion, but to them alſo that folovv the ſteppes of the faith that is in the prepuce of our father Abraham.
For not by the Lavv vvas the promiſſe to Abraham, or to his ſeede, that he ſhould be heire of the vvorld: but by the iuſtice of faith.
For if they that are of the Lavv, be heires: faith is made voide, the promiſſe is aboliſhed.
For the Lavv vvorketh vvrath. For vvhere is no lavv, neither is there preuarication.

Therfore of faith: that according to grace the promiſſe may be firme to al the ſeede, not to that only vvhich is of the Lavv, but to that alſo vvhich is of the faith of Abraham, vvho is the father of vs al,

(as it is vvritten: [1] For, a father of many nations haue I appointed thee) before God, vvhom [2] thou didſt beleeue, vvho quickeneth the dead: and calleth thoſe things that are not, as thoſe things that are.

notes.text: he believed,

verses.text: VVho contrarie to hope beleeued in hope: that he might be made the father of many nations, according to that vvhich vvas [1] ſaid to him: So ſhal thy ſeede be, as the ſtarres of heauen, and the ſand of the ſea.
And he vvas not vveakened in faith: neither did he conſider his ovvne body novv quite dead, vvhereas he vvas almoſt an hundred yeres old, and the dead matrice of Sara.
In the promiſſe alſo of God he ſtaggered not by diſtruſt: but vvas ſtrengthened in faith, giuing glorie to God:
moſt fully knovving that vvhatſoeuer he promiſed, he is able alſo to doe.
Therfore vvas it alſo reputed him to iuſtice.
And it is not vvritten only for him, that it vvas reputed him to iuſtice:
but alſo for vs, to vvhom it ſhal be reputed beleeuing in him, that raiſed vp <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc> our Lord from the dead,
vvho vvas deliuered vp for our ſinnes, and roſe againe for our iuſtification.

chapters.summary: That Abraham vvas not iuſtified by his owne power, but by Gods grace, in vvhom he beleeued (6 which is a way for the ſinner alſo to come to iuſtice.) 9 And thus, ſeing he vvas not as then circumciſed, not only the circumciſed Iewe, but alſo the vncircumciſed Gentil may by beleeuing the Chriſtian faith, come to iuſtice, as Abraham did :11 ſpecially conſidering alſo, that Abraham was promiſed to be Father of the whole world, and not only of the Iewes, to whom only the Lavv vvas giuen: and thus, not to fulfil the promis, but for an other cauſe.

verses.text: <sc>BEING</sc> <na>[1]</na> iuſtified therefore by faith, let vs haue peace tovvard God by our Lord <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc>:

notes.text: The Epiſtle on Imber Saturday in whitſon-Weeke, And for many Martyrs.

verses.text: by whom alſo vve haue acceſſe through faith into this grace vvherein vve ſtand, and glorie, <na>[1]</na> in the hope of the glorie of the ſonnes of God.

notes.text: Chriſtian mē do not vaunt thē ſelues of the certaintie of their ſaluatió, but glorie in the hope thereof onely, which hope is here inſinuated to be giuen in our iuſtificatió, & is afterward to be cōfirmed by probation in tribulation.

verses.text: And not only this: but alſo vve glorie in tribulations, knovving that tribulation vvorketh patience:
and patience probation: and probation, hope.
and hope confoundeth not: becauſe the charitie of God is povvred forth in our hartes, by the holy Ghoſt vvhich is giuen vs. ‖
For vvhy did Chriſt, vvhen vve as yet vvere <na>[1]</na> <na>[2]</na> vveake, according to the time die for the impious?

notes.text: ἀσθενῶν · The Heretikes falſely tranſlate, of no ſtrength, to take away al free wil. No. Teſt. 1580.
c ἀσθενεῖς

verses.text: For, ſcarce for a iuſt man doth any die: for perhaps for a good man durſt ſome man die.
But God commendeth his charitie in vs: becauſe, vvhen as yet vve vvere ſinners, Chriſt died for vs.
Much more therfore now being iuſtified in his bloud, ſhal vve be ſaued from vvrath by him.
For if, when vve vvere enemies, vve were reconciled to God by the death of his Sonne: much more being reconciled, ſhal vve be ſaued in the life of him.
And not only this: but alſo vve glorie in God through our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, by vvhom novv vve haue receiued reconciliation.
Therefore, as by one man ſinne entred into this vvorld, and by ſinne death: and ſo vnto al men death did paſſe, in vvhich al ſinned.
For euen vnto the Lavv ſinne vvas in the world: but ſinne was not imputed, when the law was not.
But death reigned from Adam vnto Moyſes, euen on them alſo that ſinned not after the ſimilitude of the preuarication of Adam, vvho is a figure of him to come.
But not as the offence, ſo alſo the gift. for if by the offence of one, many died: much more the grace of God and the gift, in the grace of one man <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, hath abounded vpon many.
And not as by one <na>[1]</na> <alt>ſinne</alt>, ſo alſo the gift. for iudgement in dede is of one, to condemnation: but grace is of many offences, to iuſtification.

notes.text: ſinner,

verses.text: For if in the offence of one, death reigned by one: much more they that receiue the aboundance of grace and of donation & of iuſtice, ſhal reigne in life by one, <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt.
Therfore as by the offence of one, vnto al men to condemnation: ſo alſo by the iuſtice of one, vnto al men to iuſtification of life.
For as by the diſobedience of one man, many vvere made ſinners: ſo alſo by the obedience of one, many <na>[1]</na> ſhal be made iuſt.

notes.text: Here vve may ſee againſt the Heretikes, that they which be borne of Chriſt and iuſtified by him, be made & conſtituted iuſt in dede, & not by imputation only: as al that be borne of Adam, be vniuſt and ſinners in truth, & not by imputation.

verses.text: But the Lavv entred in, that ſinne might abound. And vvhere ſinne abounded, grace did more abound.
that as ſinne reigned to death: ſo alſo grace may reigne by iuſtice to life euerlaſting, through <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt our Lord.

chapters.summary: Hauing therfore through faith in Chriſt, obteined the beginning, he ſhevveth what great cauſe vve haue to hope for the accompliſhment. 12. And then he procedeth in his arguing, and ſheweth that as by one, al were made ſinners, ſo by one, al muſt be made iuſt.

verses.text: <sc>WHAT</sc> ſhal vve ſay then? Shal vve continue in ſinne that grace may abound?
God forbid. For vve that are dead to ſinne, hovv ſhal vve yet liue therein?
b <na>[1]</na> Are you ignorant that al vve vvhich are baptized in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc>, in his death we are baptized?

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpō the 6 Sūday after Pentecoſt.

verses.text: For <na>[1]</na> we are buried together vvith him by Baptiſme into death: that as Chriſt is riſen from the dead by the glorie of the father, ſo vve alſo may vvalke in newneſſe of life.

notes.text: Remiſſion of ſinne, nevv life, ſanctification, and iuſtificatió, are giuen by baptiſme, becauſe it reſembleth in vs and applieth to vs Chriſtes death and reſurrectió, and engraffeth vs into him.

verses.text: For if we be become complanted to the ſimilitude of his death, vve ſhal be alſo of his reſurrection.
Knovving this, that our old man is crucified vvith him, that the body of ſinne may be <na>[1]</na> deſtroied, to the end that vve may ſerue ſinne no longer.

notes.text: Caſtalion noteth that Beza falſely tranſlateth enervetur, for, deſtruatur: weakened, for, deſtroyed.

verses.text: For he that is dead, is iuſtified from ſinne.
And if vve be dead vvith Chriſt, vve beleeue that vve ſhal liue alſo together vvith Chriſt.
knovving that Chriſt riſing againe from the dead, novv dieth no more, death ſhal no more haue dominion ouer him.
For that he died, to ſinne he died once: but that he liueth, he liueth to God.
So thinke you alſo, that you are dead to ſinne, but aliue to God in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord. ⊢
Let not ſinne therfore reigne in your mortal body, that you obey the concupiſcences thereof.
But neither doe ye exhibite your members inſtruments of iniquitie vnto ſinne: but exhibite your ſelues to God as of dead men, aliue: and your members inſtruments of iuſtice to God.
For ſinne ſhal not haue dominion ouer you. for you are not vnder the Lavv, but vnder grace.
VVhat then? ſhal vve ſinne, becauſe vve are not vnder the Lavv, but vnder grace? God forbid.
<cr>[1]</cr> Knovv you not that to vvhom you exhibite your ſelues ſeruants to obey, you are the ſeruants of him vvhom you obey, vvhether it be of ſinne, to death, or of obedience, to iuſtice.
But thankes be to God, that you vvere the ſeruants of ſinne, but <na>[1]</na> haue obeied from the hart, vnto that forme of doctrine, into the vvhich you haue been deliuered.

notes.text: Here againe is ſignified, that our diſcharge frō the bōdage of ſinne, is by the Chriſtian faith, & by obedience to the whole doctrine of Chriſts religion: in that the Apoſtle attributeth this their deliuerance frō ſinne, to their humble receiuing of the Catholike faith.

verses.text: And being made free from ſinne, you vvere made ſeruants to iuſtice.

<na>[1]</na> I ſpeake an humane thing, becauſe of the infirmitie of your fleſh. for as you haue exhibited your members to ſerue vncleanneſſe and iniquitie, vnto iniquitie: ſo now exhibite your members to ſerue iuſtice, <na>[2]</na> vnto ſanctification.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpō the 7 Sunday after Pentecoſt.

He ſignifieth that as when they vvere ſubiect to ſinne by cōtinual & oftē working wickednes, they increaſed their iniquitie: that ſo alſo novv being iuſtified, they may & ſhould by external vvorkes of Iuſtice, increaſe their iuſtice and ſanctification.

verses.text: For when you vvere ſeruants of ſinne, you were free to iuſtice.
VVhat fruite therfore had you then in thoſe things, for vvhich novv you are aſhamed? for the end of them is death.
But novv being made free from ſinne, and become ſeruants to God, you haue your fruite vnto ſanctification, but the end, life euerlaſting.
For the ſtipends of ſinne, death. but the grace of God, life euerlaſting in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord. ⊢

chapters.summary: He exhorteth vs, novv after Baptiſme, to liue no more in ſinne, but to walke in good vvorkes: becauſe there we died to the one, and roſe againe to the other 14 (grace alſo giuing vs ſufficient ſtrength) 16 and vvere made free to the one, and ſeruants to the other, 21 and ſpecially because of the fruite here, and the end aftervvard, both of the one and of the other.

verses.text: <sc>ARE</sc> you ignorant brethren (for I ſpeake to them that knovv the Lavv) that the Law hath dominion ouer a man as long time as <na>[1]</na> <alt>he</alt> liueth?

notes.text: it

verses.text: for <cr>[1]</cr> the vvoman that is vnder a huſband: <na>[2]</na> her huſband liuing is bound to the lavv. but if her huſband be dead, ſhe is looſed from the lavv of her huſband.

notes.text: 1. Cor. 7, 39. · Nothing but death diſſolueth the band betwixt man & wife: though for fornication one may depart from an others companie. therfore to mary againe is aduoutrie, during the life of the partie ſeparated.

verses.text: Therfore her huſband liuing, ſhe ſhal be called an aduoutereſſe if ſhe be vvith an other man: but if her huſband be dead, ſhe is deliuered from the lavv of her huſband: ſo that ſhe is not an aduoutereſſe if ſhe be vvith an other man.
Therfore my brethren <na>[1]</na> you alſo are made dead to the Lavv by the body of Chriſt: that you may be an other mans vvho is riſen againe from the dead, that vve may fructifie to God.

notes.text: Being now baptiſed and dead to ſinne, & engraffed in Chriſts myſtical body, you are diſcharged of the Lavv of Moyſes, and are free in Chriſt.

verses.text: For vvhen vve vvere in the fleſh, the paſſions of ſinnes, that vvere by the Lavv, did vvorke in our members, to fructifie vnto death.
but novv vve are looſed from the lavv of death, vvherein vve vvere deteined: c <na>[1]</na> in ſo much we ſerue in <na>[2]</na> nevvneſſe of ſpirit, and not in the oldnes of the letter.

notes.text: c ὥστε δουλεύειν
By Baptiſme we haue not Chriſtes iuſtice imputed to vs, but an inward newneſſe of ſpirit giuen vs and reſident in vs.

verses.text: VVhat ſhal we ſay then? is the Lavv ſinne? God forbid. But ſinne I did not knovv, but by the Lavv. for concupiſcence I knevv not, vnleſſe the lavv did ſay: [1] Thou ſhalt not couet.
But <na>[1]</na> occaſion being taken, ſinne by the commaundement vvrought in me al concupiſcence. For vvithout the Lavv ſinne vvas dead.

notes.text: Sinne or concupiſcence which was a ſleepe before, vvas wakened by prohibition, the Law not being the cauſe thereof, nor giuing occaſion thereunto, but occaſion being taken by our corrupt nature to reſiſt that vvhich was commaunded.

verses.text: And I liued vvithout the Lavv ſometime. But vvhen the commaundement vvas come, ſinne reuiued.
And I vvas dead: and the commaundement, that vvas vnto life, the ſame to me vvas found to be vnto death.
For ſinne taking occaſion by the commaundement, ſeduced me, and by it killed me.
Therfore <cr>[1]</cr> the Lavv in deede is holy, and the commaundement holy, and iuſt, and good.

That then vvhich is good, to me vvas it made death? God forbid. but ſinne, that it may appeare ſinne, by the good thing vvrought me death: that ſinne might become ſinning aboue meaſure by the commaundement.
For vve knovv that the Law is ſpiritual, but I am carnal, ſold vnder ſinne.
For that which I vvorke, I vnderſtand not. for not that vvhich I vvil, the ſame do I: but vvhich I hate, that I doe.
And if that vvhich I vvil not, the ſame I do: I conſent to the Lavv, that it is good.
But novv, not I vvorke it any more, but the ſinne that dvvelleth in me.
For I know that there dvvelleth not in me, that is to ſay, in my fleſh, good. For to vvil, is preſent vvith me, but to accompliſh that vvhich is good, I finde not.
For not the good vvhich I vvil, that do I: but the euil vvhich I vvil not, that I do.
And if that vvhich I vvil not, the ſame I doe: novv not I vvorke it, but the ſinne that dwelleth in me.
I finde therfore, the Lavv, to me hauing a vvil to doe good, that euil is preſent vvith me.
<na>[1]</na> For I am delighted vvith the lavv of God according to the invvard man:

notes.text: The Epiſtle in a Votiue Maſſe for ſinnes.

verses.text: but I ſee an other lavv in my members, repugning to the lavv of my minde, and captiuing me in the lavv of ſinne, that is in my members.
Vnhappie man that I am, vvho ſhal deliuer me from the body of this death?
The grace of God by <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt our Lord. ⊢ Therfore I my ſelf vvith the minde <na>[1]</na> c ſerue the lavv of God, but vvith the fleſh, the lavv of ſinne.

notes.text: c δουλεύω

chapters.summary: Our former huſband (ſinne) vvith his lavv, is dead in Baptiſme: and now we are maried to an other huſband (to Chriſt) to bring forth children to God, that is, good vvorkes. 7 And hovv the Lavv being good, vvas yet to vs the law of ſinne and death, becauſe concupiſcence reigned in vs. 17 But novv by Baptiſme grace reigneth in vs, though alſo concupiſcence doth remaine and tempt vs ſtill.

verses.text: <sc>THERE</sc> is novv therfore no damnation to them that are in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc>: that walke not according to the fleſh.
For the lavv of the ſpirit of life in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc>, hath deliuered me from the lavv of ſinne and of death.
For that vvhich vvas impoſſible to the Lavv, in that it vvas vveakened by the fleſh: God ſending his ſonne in the ſimilitude of the fleſh of ſinne, euen of ſinne damned ſinne in the fleſh,
that <na>[1]</na> the iuſtification of the lavv might be fulfilled in vs, vvho vvalke not according to the fleſh, but according to the ſpirit.

notes.text: This conuinceth againſt the Churches aduerſaries, that the law, that is, gods cōmaundemēts may be kept, & that the keeping thereof is iuſtice, & that in chriſtian men that is fulfilled by Chriſts grace vvhich by the force of the Law could neuer be fulfilled.

verses.text: For they that are according to the fleſh, are affected to the things that are of the fleſh, but they that are according to the ſpirit: are affected to the things that are of the ſpirit.
For the vviſedom of the fleſh, is death: but the vviſedom of the ſpirit, life and peace.
Becauſe the vviſedom of the fleſh, is <na>[1]</na> <alt>an enemie</alt> to God: for to the law of God it is not ſubiect, neither can it be.

notes.text: enmitie.

verses.text: And they that are in the fleſh, can not pleaſe God.
But you are not in the fleſh, but in the ſpirit, yet if the Spirit of God dvvel in you. But if any man haue not the Spirit of Chriſt, the ſame is not his.
But if Chriſt be in you: the body in deede is dead becauſe of ſinne, but the ſpirit liueth becauſe of iuſtification.

And if the Spirit of him that raiſed vp <sc>IESVS</sc> from the dead, dvvel in you: he that raiſed vp <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc> from the dead, ſhal quicken alſo your mortal bodies, becauſe of his Spirit dwelling in you.
<na>[1]</na> Therfore brethren, vve are detters: not to the fleſh, to liue according to the fleſh.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon the 8 Sunday after Pentecoſt.

verses.text: For if you liue according to the fleſh, you ſhal die. but if by the ſpirit, you mortifie the deedes of the fleſh, you ſhal liue.
For vvhoſoeuer <na>[1]</na> are ledde by the Spirit of God, they are the ſonnes of God.

notes.text: He meaneth not that the Childrē of God be violently cōpelled againſt their willes, but that they be ſweetly drawē, moued, or induced to do good. Aug. Enchirid. c. 64. De verb. Do. ſer. 43 c. 7. et de verb. Apoſt. ſer. 13 c. 11. 12.

verses.text: For <cr>[1]</cr> you haue not receiued the ſpirit of ſeruitude againe in feare: but <cr>[2]</cr> you haue receiued the ſpirit of adoption of ſonnes, vvherein vve crie: Abba, (father).
For the Spirit him ſelf, giueth teſtimonie to our ſpirit, that we are the ſonnes of God.
And if ſonnes, heires alſo: heires truly of God, and coheires of Chriſt: ⊢ yet if vve ſuffer vvith him, that vve may be alſo glorified vvith him.
<na>[1]</na> For I thinke that the paſſions of this time are not <na>[2]</na> condigne to the glorie to come that ſhal be reuealed in vs.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon the 4 Sunday after Pentecoſt, and for many Martyrs.
condignæ ad gloriam.

verses.text: For the expectation of the creature, expecteth the reuelation of the ſonnes of God.
For the creature is made ſubiect to vanitie, not vvilling, but for him that made it ſubiect in hope:
becauſe the creature alſo it ſelf ſhal be deliuered from the ſeruitude of corruption, into the libertie of the glorie of the children of God.
For vve knovv that euery creature groneth, and trauaileth euen til novv.
And not only it, but vve alſo our ſelues hauing the firſt fruites of the ſpirit, vve alſo grone vvithin our ſelues, expecting the adoption of the ſonnes of God, the redemption of our body. ⊢
For by hope vve are ſaued. But hope that is ſeen, is not hope. for that vvhich a man ſeeth, vvherfore doth he hope it?
But if vve hope for that vvhich vve ſee not: vve expect by patience.
And in like maner alſo the Spirit helpeth our infirmitie. For, vvhat vve ſhould pray as vve ought, vve knovv not: but the Spirit him ſelf requeſteth for vs vvith gronings vnſpeakeable.
And he that ſearcheth the hartes, knovveth vvhat the Spirit deſireth: becauſe according to God he requeſteth for the ſainctes.
And vve knovv that to them that loue God, al things cooperate vnto good, to ſuch as according to purpoſe are called to be ſainctes.
For vvhom he hath forknowen, he hath alſo predeſtinated to be made conformable to the image of his ſonne: that he might be the firſt-borne in many brethren.
And vvhom he hath predeſtinated: them alſo he hath called. and vvhom he hath called: them alſo he hath iuſtified. and vvhom he hath iuſtified: them alſo hath he glorified.
What ſhal vve then ſay to theſe things? If God be for vs, vvho is againſt vs?
He that ſpared not alſo his ovvne ſonne, but for vs al deliuered him: hovv hath he not alſo vvith him giuen vs al things?
Who ſhal accuſe againſt the elect of God? God that iuſtifieth.
Who is he that ſhal condemne? Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> that died, yea that is riſen alſo againe, vvho is on the right hand of God, vvho alſo maketh interceſſion for vs.
<na>[1]</na> Who then ſhal ſeparate vs from the charitie of Chriſt? tribulation? or diſtreſſe? or famine? or nakednes? or danger? or perſecution? or the ſvvord?

notes.text: The Epiſtle for S. Ignatius Febr. 1.

verses.text: (as it is vvritten, [1] For vve are killed for thy ſake al the day: vve are eſteemed as ſheepe of ſlaughter.)
But in al theſe things we ouercome becauſe of him that hath loued vs. c
<na>[1]</na> For I am ſure that neither death, nor life, nor Angels, nor Principalities, nor Povvers, neither things preſent, nor things to come, neither might,

notes.text: c πέπεισμαι γὰρ.

verses.text: nor height, nor depth, nor other creature, ſhal be able to ſeparate vs from the charitie of God vvhich is in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord. ⊢

chapters.summary: That now after Baptiſme we are no more in ſtate of damnation, because by the grace which we haue receiued, vve are able to fulfil the Law: vnles we do vvilfully giue the dominion againe to concupiſcence. 18 Then (becauſe of the perſecutions that then were) he comforteth and exhorteth them vvith many reaſons.

verses.text: <sc>I SPEAKE</sc> the verity in Chriſt, I lie not, my conſcience bearing me vvitnes in the holy Ghoſt,
that I haue great ſadneſſe & continual ſorovv in my hart.
For I vviſhed, my ſelf to be an anáthema from Chriſt for my brethren, vvho are my kinſmen according to the fleſh,
vvho are Iſraëlites, vvhoſe is the adoption of ſonnes, and the glorie, and <na>[1]</na> the teſtament, and the lavv giuing, and c the ſeruice, and the promiſſes:

notes.text: c λατρεία.

verses.text: vvhoſe are the fathers, & of vvhom Chriſt is according to the fleſh, vvho is aboue al things God bleſſed for euer. Amen.
But not that the vvord of God is fruſtrate. For, not al that are of Iſraël, they be Iſraëlites:
nor they that are the ſeede of Abraham, al be children: [1] but in Iſaac ſhal the ſeede be called vnto thee:
that is to ſay, not they that are the children of the fleſh, they are the children of God: but they that are the children of the promiſſe, are eſteemed for the ſeede.
For the word of promiſſe is this, [1] According to this time vvil I come: and Sara ſhal haue a ſonne.
<cr>[1]</cr> And not only ſhe, But <na>[2]</na> Rebecca alſo conceiuing of one copulation, of Iſaac our father.

notes.text: Al the epiſtle ſurely to the Romanes needeth interpretatiõ, and is on wrapped with ſo great obſcurities that to vnderſtãd it we neede the helpe of the Holy Ghoſt, who by the Apoſtle did dictat theſe ſame things: but eſpecially this place. Howbeit nothĩg pleaſeth vs but that which is Eccleſiaſtical, that is, the ſenſe of the Church.

verses.text: For vvhen they vvere not yet borne, nor had done any good or euil (that the purpoſe of God according to election might ſtand)
not of vvorkes, but of the caller it vvas ſaid to her: [1] That the elder ſhal ſerue the yonger,
as it is vvritten: [1] Iacob I loued, but Eſau I hated.
VVhat ſhal vve ſay then? Is there iniquitie vvith God? God forbid.
For to Moyſes he ſaith, [1] I vvil haue mercie on vvhom I haue mercie: and I vvil ſhew mercie to whom I wil ſhew mercie.
Therfore it is not of the vviller, nor the runner, but of God that ſheweth mercie.
For the Scripture ſaith to Pharao: [1] That to this very purpoſe haue I raiſed thee, that in thee I may ſhevv my povver: and that my name may be renowmed in the vvhole earth.
Therfore on vvhom he vvil, he hath mercie: and vvhom he vvil, he doth indurate.
Thou ſaieſt therfore vnto me: VVhy doth he yet complaine? for vvho reſiſteth his vvil?
O man, vvho art thou that doeſt anſvver God? Doth the vvorke ſay to him that vvrought it: VVhy haſt thou made me thus?
Or hath not the potter of clay, povver, of the ſame maſſe to make one veſſel vnto honour, and an other vnto contumelie?
And if God vvilling to ſhevv vvrath, and to make his might knovven, <na>[1]</na> ſuſteined in much patience the veſſels of wrath <na>[2]</na> <alt>`apte</alt>' to deſtruction,

notes.text: That God is not the cauſe of any mans reprobation or damnation, othervviſe then for puniſhment of his ſinnes, he ſheweth by that he expecteth al mens amendement with great patience, and conſequently that they haue alſo free wil.
`apted, fitted.

verses.text: that he might ſhevv the riches of his glorie vpon the veſſels of mercie vvhich he prepared vnto glorie.
VVhom alſo he hath called, vs, not only of the Ievves, but alſo of the Gentiles,
as in Oſee he ſaith, [1] I wil call that which is not my people, my people: and her that vvas not beloued, beloued: and her that hath not obteined mercie, hauing obteined mercie.
[1] And it ſhal be, in the place vvhere it vvas ſaid to them, you are not my people: there they ſhal be called the ſonnes of the liuing God.
And Eſaie crieth for Iſrael, [1] If the number of the children of Iſrael be as the ſand of the ſea, the remaines ſhal be ſaued.
For, conſummating a word, and abbridging it in equitie: becauſe a vvord abbridged ſhal our Lord make vpon the earth.
And as Eſay foretold, [1] Vnles the Lord of Sabaoth had left vs ſeede: vve had been made like Sodom, and vve had been like as Gomorrha.
What ſhal vve ſay then? That the Gentiles vvhich purſued not after iuſtice, haue apprehended iuſtice, but the iuſtice that is of faith.
But Iſrael in purſuing the lavv of iuſtice, is not come vnto the lavv of iuſtice.
VVhy ſo? Becauſe not of faith, but as it vvere of vvorkes. for c <na>[1]</na> they haue ſtombled at the ſtone of ſtombling,

notes.text: c Here we ſee that they are the cauſe of their owne damnation by infidelity.

verses.text: as it is vvritten, [1] Behold I put in Sion a ſtone of ſtombling, and a rocke of ſcandal: and vvhoſoeuer beleeueth in him, ſhal not be confounded.

notes.text: In all this mercy of God towards ſome, and juſtice tovvards other ſome, both the pardoned work by their own free-will, and thereby deſerve their ſalvation: and the other no leſs, by their own free-will, vvithout all neceſſity, work wickedneſs, & themſelves and only of themſelves procure their own damnation. Therefore no man may vvithout blaſphemy ſay, or can truly ſay, that he hath nothing to do towards his own ſalvation, but will live, and thinketh he may live vvithout care or cogitation of his end the one vvay or the other, ſaying, If I be appointed to be ſaved, be it ſo: if I be one deſigned to damnation, I cannot help the matter: come vvhat come may. All theſe ſpeeches and cogitations are ſinful & come of the enemy, and be rather ſigns of reprobation, than of election. Therefore the good man muſt vvithout ſearch of God's ſecrets, work his own ſalvation and (as S. Peter ſaith

chapters.summary: With a proteſtation of his ſorow for it (leſt they ſhould thinke him to reioyce in their perdition) he inſinuateth the Iewes to be reprobate, although they come of Abrahams fleſh, 6 ſaying, to be the ſonnes of God, goeth not by that, but by Gods grace: 19 conſidering that al vvere one damned maſſe. 24 by which grace the Gentils to be made his people: and ſo the prophets to haue foretold of them both. 30 And the cauſe hereof to be, that the Gentils ſubmit them ſelues to the faith of Chriſt, which the Iewes vvil not.

verses.text: <sc>BRETHREN</sc>, the vvil of my hart ſurely and praier to God, is for them vnto ſaluation.
For I giue them teſtimonie that they haue zeale of God, but not according to knowledge.
For, not knovving the iuſtice of God, & ſeeking to eſtabliſh their ovvne, they haue not been ſubiect to the iuſtice of God.
For, <na>[1]</na> the end of the Law is Chriſt: vnto iuſtice to euery one that beleeueth.

notes.text: The Law was not giuen to make a man iuſt or perfect by it ſelf, but to bring vs to Chriſt to be iuſtified by him.

verses.text: For Moyſes vvrote, [1] that, the iuſtice vvhich is of the Lavv, [2] the man that hath done it, ſhal liue in it.

notes.text: The iuſtice of the Law of Moyſes went no further of it ſelf, but to ſaue a man from the temporal death and puniſhment preſcribed to the tranſgreſſors of the ſame.

verses.text: But the iuſtice vvhich is of faith, ſaith thus, [1] Say not in thy hart, Who ſhal aſcend into heauen? that is to bring Chriſt dovvne.
Or vvho deſcendeth into the depth? that is to call Chriſt againe from the dead.
But vvhat ſaith the Scripture? The vvord is nigh, in thy mouth, and in thy hart. this is the vvord of faith vvhich vve preach.
For if thou confeſſe vvith thy mouth our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc>, and in thy hart beleeue that God hath raiſed him vp from the dead, thou ſhalt be ſaued.
<na>[1]</na> For vvith the hart vve beleeue vnto iuſtice: but vvith the mouth confeſſion is made to ſaluation.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon S. Andrewes day, Nouemb. 30.

verses.text: For the Scripture ſaith: [1] Whoſoeuer beleeueth in him, ſhal not be confounded.
For there is no diſtinction of the Iew and the Greeke: for one is Lord of al, riche tovvard al that inuocate him.
[1] For euery one [2] vvhoſoeuer ſhal inuocate the name of our Lord, ſhal be ſaued.

notes.text: To beleeue in him & to inuocate him, is to ſerue him with al loue and ſincere affectiō. Al that ſo doe, ſhal doubtleſſe be ſaued & ſhal neuer be confounded.

verses.text: Hovv then ſhal they inuocate in vvhom they haue not beleeued? Or hovv ſhal they beleeue him vvhom they haue not heard? And hovv ſhal they heare without a preacher?
But hovv ſhal they preach vnles they be ſent? as it is vvritten: [1] Hovv beautiful are the feete of them that euangelize peace, of them that euangelize good things?
But al <cr>[1]</cr> do not obey the Goſpel. For Eſay ſaith, Lord, vvho hath beleeued the hearing of vs?

notes.text: We ſee then that it is in a mans free vvil to beleeue or not to beleeue, to obey or diſobey the Goſpel or truth preached.

verses.text: Faith then, is by hearing: and heating is by the vvord of Chriſt.
But I ſay, haue they not heard? And certes [1] into al the earth hath the ſound of them gone forth: and vnto the endes of the vvhole world the vvordes of them. ⊢
But I ſay, hath not Iſrael knovven? Moyſes firſt ſaith, [1] I vvil bring you to emulation in that vvhich is not a nation: in a foliſh nation I vvil driue you into anger.
But Eſay is bold, and ſaith, [1] I was found of them that did not ſeeke me: openly I appeared to them that aſked not of me.
But to Iſrael he ſaith, [1] Al the day haue I ſpred my handes to a people that beleeueth not, and contradicteth me.

chapters.summary: The Law vvas not (as the Iewes ignorant zeale ſuppoſed) for them to iuſtifie them ſelues by it (conſidering that they could not fulfil it:) but to bring them to Chriſt to beleeue in him, and ſo for his ſake to be iuſtified by the grace of God: 5 according to Moyſes ſaying, and the Apoſtles preaching: 11 that ſo the Gentils alſo (according to the Prophets) hearing and beleeuing might come to iuſtice: the Iewes in the meane time (though inexcuſably) remaining incredulous.

verses.text: <sc>I Say</sc> then: Hath God reiected his people? God forbid. for I alſo am an Iſraelite, of the ſeede of Abraham, of the tribe of Ben-iamin.
God hath not reiected his people vvhich he foreknevve. Or knovv you not in Elias vvhat the Scripture ſaith: hovv he requeſteth God againſt Iſraël?
[1] Lord, they haue ſlaine thy Prophets, they haue digged dovvne thine altares: and I am left alone, and they ſeeke my life.
But vvhat ſaith the diuine anſvver vnto him? I haue left me ſeuen thouſand men, that haue not bovved their knees to [1] Baal?

notes.text: c The Heretics adde here alſo, Image, to the text, as Act. 19, 35.

verses.text: So therfore at this time alſo, there are remaines ſaued according to the election of grace.
And if by grace: not novv of vvorkes. othervviſe grace now is not grace.
What then? that vvhich Iſrael ſought, the ſame he hath not obtained: but the election hath obtained: and the reſt vvere blinded.
as it is vvritten: [1] God hath giuen them the ſpirit of compunction: eies, that they may not ſee: and eares, that they may not heare: vntil this preſent day.
And Dauid ſaith: [1] Be their table made for a ſnare and for a trappe and for a ſcandal and for a retribution vnto them.
Be their eies darkened, that they may not ſee: and their backe make thou alvvaies crooked.
I ſay then, haue they ſo ſtombled, <na>[1]</na> that they ſhould fall? God forbid. but by their offence, ſaluation is to the Gentils, that they may emulate them.

notes.text: The Iewes are not reiected wholly & incurably for euer: but for a part, and for a time ſuffered to fall. Which God did turne to the Gentils general good.

verses.text: And if the offence of them be the riches of the vvorld, and the diminution of them <na>[1]</na> the riches of the Gentils: hovv much more the fulneſſe of them?

notes.text: If God could and did turne their fall and ſinne into the good of the Gentils, much more wil he worke good of their general conuerſion, which ſhalbe at length the accompliſhment of the Church conſiſting of both the Nations.

verses.text: For to you Gentils I ſay, as long verely as I am the Apoſtle of the Gentils, I vvil honour my miniſterie,
if by any meanes I may prouoke my fleſh to emulation, and may ſaue ſome of them.
For if the loſſe of them be the reconciliation of the vvorld: vvhat ſhal the receiuing be, but life from the dead?
And if the firſt fruite be holy, the maſſe alſo: and if the roote be holy, the boughes alſo.
And if ſome of the boughes be broken, and thou vvhereas thou vvaſt a vvilde oliue, art graffed in them, and art made partaker of the roote and of the fatneſſe of the oliue,
glorie not againſt the boughes. And if thou glorie: not thou beareſt the roote, but the roote thee.
Thou ſaieſt then: The boughes were broken, that I might be graffed in.
Vvel: becauſe of incredulitie they vvere broken, but thou by faith doeſt ſtand: be not to highly vviſe, but <na>[1]</na> feare.

notes.text: We ſee that he which ſtandeth by faith, may fall from it, and therfore muſt liue in feare, and not in the vaine preſumption and ſecuritie of the Heretikes.

verses.text: For if God hath not ſpared the natural boughes: leſt perhaps he vvil not ſpare thee neither.
See then the goodnes and the ſeueritie of God: vpon them ſurely that are fallen, the ſeueritie: but vpon thee the goodnes of God, if thou abide in his goodneſſe, othervviſe thou alſo ſhalt be cut of.
But they alſo, if they do not abide in incredulitie, ſhal be graffed in. for God is able to graffe them in againe.

For if thou waſt cut out of the natural vvild oliue, and contrarie to nature waſt graffed into the good oliue: hovv much more they that are according to nature, ſhal be graffed into their ovvne oliue?
For I vvil not haue you ignorant, brethren, of this myſterie (that you be not wiſe in your ſelues) that blindnes in part hath chaunced in Iſraël, vntil the fulnes of the Gentiles might enter:
and ſo al Iſraël might be ſaued, as it is vvritten: [1] There shal come out of Sion, he that ſhal deliuer, and ſhal auert impietie from Iacob.
And this to them the teſtament from me: vvhen I ſhal haue taken avvay their ſinnes.
According to the Goſpel in deede enemies for you: but according to the election, moſt deere for the fathers.
for vvithout repentance are the giftes and the vocation of God.
for as you alſo ſometime did not beleeue God, but novv haue obteined mercie becauſe of their incredulitie:
ſo theſe alſo novv haue not beleeued, for your mercie, that they alſo may obteine mercie.
For God hath concluded al into incredulitie, that he may haue mercie on al.
<na>[1]</na> O depth of the riches of the vviſedom and of the knowledge of God: hovv incomprehenſible are his iudgements, and his vvaies vnſearcheable?

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon Trinitie Sunday.

verses.text: for <cr>[1]</cr> vvho hath knovven the minde of our Lord? Or vvho hath been his counſeler?
Or vvho hath firſt giuen to him, and retribution ſhal be made him?
For of him, and by him, and in him are al things: to him be glorie for euer. Amen. ⊢

chapters.summary: Not al the Iewes vvere reprobate, but ſome electe: and they by grace obtained iuſtice, the reſt (according to the Prophets) being excecated. 11 Againſt whom notwithſtanding the Chriſtian Gentils (to whom by that occaſion Chriſt is come) muſt not inſult: but rather feare euery man him ſelf to be likewiſe cut of the tree (vvhich is the Catholike Church) 25 and know that when al the Gentils are brought into the Church, then (about the end of the vvorld) ſhal the multitude of the Ievves alſo come in: 33 according to the diſpoſition of the wonderful wiſedom of God.

verses.text: I <cr>[1]</cr> <sc>BESECH</sc> you therfore brethren by the mercie of God, <na>[2]</na> that you exhibite your bodies a liuing hoſt, holy, pleaſing God, your reaſonable ſeruice.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon the 2 Sunday after the Epiphanie.

verses.text: And be not conformed to this vvorld: but be reformed in the newnes of your minde, <cr>[1]</cr> that you may proue vvhat the good, and acceptable, and perfect vvil of God is.

for I ſay by the grace that is giuen me, to al that are among you, <cr>[1]</cr> not to be more vviſe then behoueth to be vviſe, but to be vviſe vnto ſobrietie, <na>[2]</na> to euery one as God hath deuided the meaſure of faith.

notes.text: None muſt preſume to medle aboue the meaſure of gods gift, or out of the compaſſe of his ſtate and vocation. · 1.Cor. 12, 11. Eph. 4, 7.

verses.text: For as in one body vve haue many members, but al the members haue not one action:
ſo vve being many, are one body in Chriſt, & eche one an others members. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> And hauing giftes, according to the grace that is giuen vs, different: either <na>[2]</na> prophecie according to the rule of faith,

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon the 2 Sunday after the Epiphanie.

Prophecie is interpretation of the Scriptures, which is according to the rule of faith, when it is not againſt the right faith, or when it is profitable to edifie charitie, as S. Auguſtine ſpeaketh li. 3. Doct. Chr. c. 27 and li. 1. c. 36. and in effect he ſaith the ſame li. 12. Confeſs. c. 18 vnto c. 32.

verses.text: or miniſterie in miniſtring, or he that teacheth in doctrine,
he that exhorteth in exhorting, he that giueth in ſimplicitie, he that ruleth in carefulnes, he that ſhevveth mercie in cheerefulnes.
<na>[1]</na> Loue vvithout ſimulation. Hating euil. cleauing to good.

notes.text: c dilectio

verses.text: Louing the charitie of the brotherhod one toward an other. VVith honour preuenting one an other.
In carefulnes not ſlouthful. In ſpirit feruent. Seruing our Lord.
Reioycing in hope. Patient in tribulation. Inſtant in praier.
Communicating to the <na>[1]</na> <alt>neceſſities</alt> of the ſainctes. Purſuing hoſpitalitie.

notes.text: memories

verses.text: Bleſſe them that perſecute you: bleſſe, and <na>[1]</na> curſe not.

notes.text: Curſing is a vice whereunto the common people is much giuen, who often curſe them on whom they can not otherwiſe be reuenged. they may ſee here that it is a great fault.

verses.text: To reioyce vvith them that reioyce, to vveepe vvith them that vveepe.
Being of one minde one tovvard an other. Not minding high things, but conſenting to the humble. ⊢ <na>[1]</na> Be not vviſe in your ovvne conceite.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon the 3 Sunday after the Epiphanie.

verses.text: To no man rendring euil for euil. Prouiding good things not only before God, but alſo before al men.
If it may be, as much as is in you, hauing peace vvith al men.
Not reuenging your ſelues my deereſt, but giue place vnto vvrath, for it is vvritten: [1] Reuenge to me: I vvil revvard, ſaith our Lord.
but [1] if thine enemie hunger, giue him meate: if he thirſt, giue him drinke. for, doing this, thou ſhalt heape coales of fire vpon his head.
Be not ouercome of euil, but ouercome in good the euil. ⊢

chapters.summary: He exhorteth them to mortification of the body, 2 to renouation of the minde, 3 to keeping of vnitie by humilitie, 6 to the right vſing of their gifts and functions, 9 to many other good actions, 17 and ſpecially to louing of their enemies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The ſecond part of this Epiſtle, moral.

verses.text: LET <cr>[1]</cr> euery ſoul be ſubiect to higher powers, for there is no povver but of God. And thoſe that are, of God are ordeined.
Therfore he that reſiſteth the povver, reſiſteth the ordinance of God. And they that reſiſt, purchaſe to them ſelues damnation.
for princes are no feare to the good worke, but to the euil. But wilt thou not feare the povver? Doe good: and thou ſhalt haue praiſe of the ſame.
for he is gods miniſter vnto thee for good. But if thou doe euil, feare. for he beareth not the ſvvord without cauſe. For he is Gods miniſter: a reuenger vnto vvrath, to him that doeth euil.
Therfore be ſubiect of neceſſitie, not only for vvrath, but alſo for conſcience ſake.
For therefore you giue tributes alſo. for they are the miniſters of God, ſeruing vnto this purpoſe.
<cr>[1]</cr> Render therfore to al men their devv: <na>[2]</na> to vvhom tribute, tribute: to vvhom cuſtom, cuſtom: to whom feare, feare: to vvhom honour, honour.

notes.text: Obedience to temporal rulers, & in what caſes.

verses.text: Ovve no man any thing: but, that you loue one an other. For he that loueth his neighbour, hath <na>[1]</na> fulfilled the lavv.

notes.text: Here vve learne that the Law may be & is fulfilled by loue in this life: againſt the Aduerſaries ſaying it is impoſſible to keepe the commaundements.

verses.text: for, [1] Thou ſhalt not commit aduoutrie, Thou ſhalt not kil, Thou ſhalt not ſteale, Thou ſhalt not beare falſe vvitnes, Thou ſhalt not couet, and if there be any other commaundement: it is compriſed in this vvord, [2] Thou ſhalt loue thy neighbour as thy ſelf.
The loue of thy neighbour, vvorketh no euil. Loue therfore is the fulneſſe of the lavv. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> And that knovving the ſeaſon, that it is novv the houre for vs to riſe from ſleepe. For novv our ſaluation is neerer then vvhen vve beleeued.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpon the 1 Sunday in Aduent.

verses.text: The night is paſſed, and the day is at hand. Let vs therfore caſt of the vvorkes of darkneſſe, and doe on the armour of light.
As in the day let vs vvalke honeſtly: not in banketings and drunkennes, not in chamberings and impudicities, not in contention and emulation:
but doe ye on our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, ⊢ and make not prouiſion for the fleſh in concupiſcences.

chapters.summary: To yeld obedience and al other duties vnto Poteſtats: 8 to loue their neighbour vvhich is the fulfilling of the Lavv: 11 and ſpecially to conſider, that novv being the time of grace, vve muſt doe nothing that may not beſeme day light.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> him that is vveake in faith, take vnto you: not in diſputations of cogitations.
For one beleeueth that he may eate al things: but he that is vveake, <na>[1]</na> <alt>let him eate</alt> herbes.

notes.text: eateth

verses.text: Let not him that eateth, deſpiſe him that eateth not: and he that eateth not: let him not iudge him that eateth. for God hath taken him to him.
VVho art thou that iudgeſt an other mans ſeruant? To his ovvne Lord he ſtandeth or falleth. and he ſhal ſtand: for God is able to make him ſtand.
For one iudgeth betvveene day and day: and an other iudgeth euery day. let euery one abound in his ovvne ſenſe.
He that reſpecteth the day, reſpecteth to our Lord. And he that eateth, eateth to our Lord: for he giueth thankes to God. And he that eateth not, to our Lord he eateth not, and giueth thankes to God.
For none of vs liueth to him ſelf: & no man dieth to him ſelf.
For whether vve liue, we liue to our Lord: or vvhether we die, we die to our Lord. Therfore vvhether vve liue, or vvhether vve die, vve are our Lords.
For to this end Chriſt died and roſe againe: that he may haue dominion both of the dead and of the liuing.
But thou, vvhy iudgeſt thou thy brother? or thou, vvhy doeſt thou deſpiſe thy brother? For <cr>[1]</cr> vve ſhal al ſtand before the iudgement ſeate of Chriſt.
For it is vvritten, Liue I, ſaith our Lord, [1] that euery knee ſhal bovve to me: and euery tongue ſhal confeſſe to God.
Therfore euery one of vs for him ſelf ſhal render account to God.
Let vs therfore no more iudge one an other. but this iudge ye rather, that you put not a ſtumbling blocke or a ſcandal to your brother.
I knovv and am perſuaded in our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, that nothing is <na>[1]</na> common of it ſelf, but to him that ſuppoſeth, any thing to be common, to him it is common.

notes.text: Common, that is, vncleane. See Annot. Marc. 7, 2.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> For if becauſe of meate thy brother be greeued: novv thou vvalkeſt not according to charitie. <na>[2]</na> Do not vvith thy meate deſtroy him for vvhom Chriſt died.

notes.text: Though he vviſh the vveake to be borne withal, yet he vttereth his minde plainly, that in deede al the meates forbidden and vncleane in the Law, are now through Chriſt cleanſed & lawful for euery man to vſe.

verses.text: Let not then our good be blaſphemed.
For the kingdom of God is not meate and drinke: but iuſtice, and peace, and ioy in the holy Ghoſt.
For he that in this ſerueth Chriſt, pleaſeth God, and is acceptable to men.
Therfore the things that are of peace let vs purſue: and the things that are of edifying one tovvard an other let vs keepe.
Deſtroy not the vvorke of God for meate. <cr>[1]</cr> Al things in deede are cleane: but it is il for the man that eateth by giuing offence.
It is good not to eate fleſh, and not to drinke vvine, nor that vvherein thy brother is offended, or ſcandalized, or vveakened.
Haſt thou faith? haue it with thy ſelf before God. Bleſſed is he that iudgeth not him ſelf in that vvhich he approueth.
But he that diſcerneth, if he eate, is damned: becauſe not of faith. for al that is not of faith, is ſinne.

chapters.summary: Like a moderator and peacemaker betwene the firme Chriſtians (who were the Gentils) and the infirme (who were the Chriſtian Iewes, hauing yet a ſcruple to ceaſe from keeping the ceremonial meates and daies of Moyſes Law) he exhorteth the Iew not to condemne the Gentil vſing his libertie: and the Gentil againe, not to condemne the ſcrupulous Iew: but rather to abſtaine from vſing his libertie, then offending the Iew, to be an occaſion vnto him of apoſtating.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> vve that are the ſtronger, muſt ſuſteine the infirmities of the vveake, & not pleaſe our ſelues.
Let euery one of you pleaſe his neighbour vnto good, to edification.
For, Chriſt did not pleaſe him ſelf, but as it is vvritten, [1] The reproches of them that reproched thee, fel vpon me.
<na>[1]</na> For <na>[2]</na> vvhat things ſoeuer haue been vvritten, to our learning they are vvritten: that by the patience and conſolation of the Scriptures, vve may haue hope.

notes.text: The Epiſtle vpō the 2. Sunday in Aduent.
He meaneth al that is vvritten in the old Teſtamēt: much more al things written in the new Teſtamēt, are for our learning and comfort.

verses.text: And the God of patience and of comfort giue you to be of one minde one tovvard an other according to <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt:
that of <na>[1]</na> one minde, vvith one mouth you may glorifie God and the Father of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt.

notes.text: c Vnitie in religion commended.

verses.text: For the vvhich cauſe receiue one an other: as Chriſt alſo hath receiued you vnto the honour of God.
For I ſay Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> to haue been <na>[1]</na> miniſter of the circumciſion for the veritie of God, to confirme the promiſſes of the fathers.

notes.text: Chriſt did execute his office and miniſterie onely towards the people of Circumciſion, that is, the Iewes.

verses.text: But the Gentils to honour God for his mercie, as it is vvritten: [1] Therfore vvil I confeſſe to thee in the Gentils ô Lord, and vvil ſing to thy name.
And againe he ſaith, [1] Reioyce ye Gentils vvith his people.
And againe, [1] Praise al ye Gentils our Lord: and magnifie him al ye peoples.
And againe Eſaie ſaith, [1] There ſhal be the roote of Ieſſe: and he that ſhal riſe vp to rule the Gentils, in him the Gentils ſhal hope.
And the God of hope repleniſh you vvith al ioy and peace in beleeuing: that you may abound in hope, and in the vertue of the holy Ghoſt. ⊢
And I my ſelf alſo, my brethren, am aſſured of you, that you alſo are ful of loue, repleniſhed vvith al knowledge, ſo that you are able to admoniſh one an other.
But I haue vvritten to you (brethren) more boldly in part, as it were putting you in remembrance: for the grace vvhich is giuen me of God,
to be the miniſter of Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> in the Gentils: ſanctifying the Goſpel of God, that the oblation of the Gentils may be made acceptable and ſanctified in the holy Ghoſt.
I haue therfore glorie in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc> toward God.
For I dare not ſpeake any of thoſe things vvhich Chriſt vvorketh not by me for the obedience of the Gentils, by vvord and deedes,
in the vertue of ſignes and wonders, in the vertue of the holy Ghoſt: ſo that from Hieruſalem round about vnto Illyricum I haue repleniſhed the Goſpel of Chriſt.
And I haue ſo preached this Goſpel, not vvhere Chriſt vvas named, leſt I ſhould build vpon an other mans foundation:
but as it is vvritten, [1] They to vvhom it hath not been preached of him, ſhal ſee: and they that haue not heard, ſhal vnderſtand.
For the vvhich cauſe alſo I vvas hindred very much from comming vnto you.
But now hauing no longer place in theſe countries, and hauing a deſire to come vnto you theſe many yeres novv paſſed:
vvhen I ſhal begin to take my iourney into Spaine, I hope that as I paſſe, I ſhal ſee you, and be brought thither of you, if firſt in part I ſhal haue enioyed you.
Now therfore I vvil goe vnto Hieruſalem to miniſter to the <na>[1]</na> ſaincts.

notes.text: He meaneth the holy perſons that hauing forſaken al their goods for Chriſt, vvere vvholy conuerted to ſerue our Lord with al their minde. S. Hiero. againſt Vigilantius the Heretike reprehending the almes giuen to ſuch, as do the Heretikes alſo of our time.

verses.text: For Macedonia and Achaia haue liked vvel to make ſome contribution vpon the poore ſaincts that are in Hieruſalem.
For it hath pleaſed them: and they are their detters. For if the Gentiles be made partakers of their ſpiritual things: they ought alſo in carnal things to miniſter vnto them.
This therfore vvhen I ſhal haue accompliſhed, and ſigned them this fruite, I vvil goe by you into Spaine.
And I knovv that comming to you, I ſhal come in aboundance of the bleſſing of Chriſt.
I beſeeche you therfore brethren by our Lord <sc>IESVS Chriſt</sc>, and by the charitie of the holy Ghoſt, that you <na>[1]</na> helpe me in your praiers for me to God,

notes.text: In that the Apoſtle deſired to be praied for, vve may be moued to ſeeke the ſame as a great benefite.

verses.text: that I may be deliuered from the infidels that are in Ievvrie, and the oblation of my ſeruice may become acceptable in Hieruſalem to the ſaincts,
that I may come to you in ioy by the vvil of God, that I may be refreſhed vvith you.
And the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

chapters.summary: He proceedeth to make peace betwene the Chriſtian Gentils and Iewes. 8 vvith this reſolution, that the Iewes vocation is of promis in deede, but the Gentils alſo of mercie, and foretold by the Scriptures. 14 Then dravving to an ende, he excuſeth him ſelf to the Romanes for writing thus vnto them, 21 hoping now at length to ſee them, after that he hath been at Hieruſalem, 29 wherevnto alſo he requeſteth their praiers.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> I commend to you Phœbè our ſiſter, vvho is in the miniſterie of the Church that is in Cenchris:
that you receiue her in our Lord as it is vvorthie for ſaincts: and that you aſſiſt her in whatſoeuer buſines ſhe ſhal neede you. for ſhe alſo hath aſſiſted many and my ſelf.
<na>[1]</na> Salute Priſca and Aquila my helpers in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc>,

notes.text: c The onely ſalutation of ſo vvorthy a man is ſufficient to fil him with greate grace that is ſo ſaluted. Chryſ. in 2. Tim. 4.

verses.text: ( vvho for my life haue laid dovvne their neckes: to whom not I only giue thankes, but alſo al the Churches of the Gentiles)
and their <na>[1]</na> domeſtical Church. Salute Epænetus my beloued: vvho is the firſt fruite of Aſia in Chriſt.

notes.text: This domeſtical Church was either that faithful and Chriſtian houſhold, or rather the Chriſtians meeting together there & in ſuch good houſes to heare diuine ſeruice and the Apoſtles preaching in thoſe times of perſecution.

verses.text: Salute Marie vvho hath laboured much about vs.
Salute Andrónicus and <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘Iulia</alt>’ my coſins and fellovv captiues: vvho are noble among the Apoſtles, vvho alſo before me vvere in Chriſt.

notes.text: Iunia

verses.text: Salute Ampliátus my beſt beloued in our Lord.
Salute Vrbánus our helper in Chriſt <sc>IESVS</sc>, and Stachys my beloued.
Salute Apelles <na>[1]</na> approued in Chriſt. Salute them that are of Ariſtóbolus houſe.

notes.text: c τὸν δόκιμον

verses.text: Salute Herodion my kinſman. Salute them that are of Narciſſus houſe, that are in our Lord.
Salute Tryphæna and Tryphóſa: vvho labour in our Lord. Salute Perſis the beloued, vvho hath much laboured in our Lord.
Salute Rufus the elect in our Lord and his mother and mine.
<na>[1]</na> Salute Aſyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Pátrobas, Hermes: and the brethren that are vvith them.

notes.text: The Proteſtants here reaſon thus, Peter is not here ſaluted, therfore he was neuer at Rome. See the Annotation.

verses.text: Salute Philólogus and Iulia, Nereus, and his ſiſter and Olympias: and al the ſaincts that are vvith them.
Salute one an other in a holy kiſſe. Al the churches of Chriſt ſalute you.
And I deſire you brethren, to marke them that make diſſenſions and ſcandals contrarie to the doctrine vvhich you haue <na>[1]</na> learned, and auoid them.

notes.text: c Of the Prince of the Apoſtles, ſaith Theodorete vpon this place.

verses.text: For ſuch doe not ſerue Chriſt our Lord, but their ovvne belly: and <na>[1]</na> by ſvveete ſpeaches and benedictions ſeduce the hartes of innocents.

notes.text: The ſpecial way that Heretikes haue euer had to beguile, vvas and is by ſweete vvordes & gay ſpeaches. Which their ſheepes cote ſee before deſcribed particularly in the Annotations vpon S. Matthew. c. 7, 15.

verses.text: For your obedience is publiſhed into euery place. I reioyce therfore in you. But I vvould haue you to be vviſe in good, and ſimple in euil.
And the God of peace cruſh Satan vnder your feete quickely. The grace of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt be vvith you.
Timothee my coadiutor ſaluteth you, and Lucius, and Iaſon, and Soſípater, my kinſmen.
I Tertius ſalute you, that vvrote the epiſtle, in our Lord.
Caius mine hoſt, and the whole Churches, ſaluteth you. Eraſtus the Cofferer of the citie ſaluteth you, and Quartus, a brother.
The grace of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt be vvith al you, Amen.
And to him that is able to confirme you according to my Goſpel and preaching of <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, according to the reuelation of the myſterie from eternal times kept ſecrete,
vvhich novv is opened by the Scriptures of the prophets according to the precept of the eternal God, to the obedience of faith knovven in al Gentiles,
to God the only vviſe through <sc>IESVS</sc> Chriſt, ‘to vvhom’ be honour & glorie for euer and euer. Amen.

chapters.summary: He commendeth the bearer Phœbè to the Romanes, 3 and him ſelf to many there by name. 17 he declareth the doctrine vvhich the Romanes had learned, to be the touchſtone to know Seducers. 21 he doth vnto them the commendations of al the Churches and of certaine perſons by name: 25 and concludeth.
